subject: Request: temporary uptime tolerance for Vision Prototype rollout
messages:
From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@horizonhealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Health Procurement <procurement@horizonhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot load and uptime tolerance ask

Hi Priya —

As discussed in the call this morning, we’re going to start a week-long synthetic load exercise for the Vision Prototype (internal name: HV-vision). The test will exercise longer sequences and burst traffic that’s representative of our Admin/Analytics use case. Our engineering team expects a small number of transient outages during heavy KV-cache warmup and when we switch the canary routing policy.

Would Redwood be able to grant a temporary uptime tolerance window for the pilot (7/20–7/26) to avoid automatic SLA penalties while we validate model stability? We’re happy to accept explicit rollback triggers and share live Grafana links. I’ve attached the rough load plan (loadplan.xlsx).

Key asks:
- Temporary uptime tolerance (up to 99.0% for the window)
- Agreement on rollback triggers (latency > 2s p95 for 15m, or error rate > 5%)
- Daily check-ins + monitoring access

Appreciate a quick confirmation so our SREs can proceed with the traffic schedule.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Kim
SRE Lead, Horizon Health
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot load and uptime tolerance ask

Thanks Daniel — and thanks for the load plan.

Short answer: we can support a temporary accommodation for pilot testing, but we need to lock in explicit conditions and an internal approval path before greenlighting any SLA carve-out. I’m looping in Marissa and Ben to get a sign-off on the operational mitigations and any commercial impact (credits, addendum).

Could you confirm the following so we can move fast:
- Exact traffic start window (UTC) and expected p50/p95/p99 latencies under baseline
- Are you planning any model variant switches during the window? (fallback model recommended)
- Who will be the on-call point-of-contact at Horizon during business hours and nights?

We’ll aim to provide an initial signed addendum (PDF) and a short set of rollback/monitoring triggers by EOD tomorrow.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T09:58:00-07:00
Subject: internal: proposed temporary uptime tolerance language + ops mitigations

Folks — drafting the internal language and ops plan we can present to Horizon. My notes below (quick bullets). I recommend approval with these constraints.

Proposed temporary tolerance (language for addendum):
- Effective window: 2028-07-20T00:00:00Z through 2028-07-26T23:59:59Z
- Temporary Service Availability Target: 99.0% (measured per calendar-day)
- Participation: Applies only to HV-vision model endpoints associated with Horizon Health account DEAL-4789
- Outages caused by misconfiguration or human error on Horizon’s side are excluded (standard clause)

Operational mitigations we will apply:
- Pre-warm KV caches and run synthetic traffic 2 hours before live window
- Route traffic to a conservative fallback variant (vision-small-quant) on latency spike
- Enable aggressive prefix caching for analytics queries
- 24/7 on-call schedule for Redwood infra (primary: infra-ops, secondary: runtime-eng)

Rollback triggers (automatic):
- p95 latency > 2.0s for a rolling 15-minute window across region
- error rate (5xx) > 5% for 10 minutes
- sustained degradation > 30 minutes without mitigation

Commercial notes:
- We can waive SLA credits for the window if Horizon agrees to the rollback triggers and provides monitoring access and a daily sync (15m). If they refuse rollback or monitoring, we should escalate to legal for a formal amendment that includes compensation.

Attachments suggested to send: redwood-uptime-addendum-v1.pdf (draft)

If Ben/ Priya are good with the window and triggers I’ll finalize the PDF and route to Legal for a quick review.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@horizonhealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-21T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot load and uptime tolerance ask

Daniel — thanks for the patience. We’ve approved a temporary uptime tolerance for the Vision Prototype pilot on the terms below. Please consider this message our confirmation pending the signed addendum (linked).

Approved terms (summary):
- Window: 2028-07-20 00:00 UTC – 2028-07-26 23:59 UTC
- Temporary availability target: 99.0% measured daily for the covered endpoints (HV-vision for DEAL-4789)
- Rollback triggers: p95 latency > 2.0s (15m), 5xx > 5% (10m), sustained > 30m
- Monitoring: Horizon to provide Grafana read-only links + a primary on-call (we have their contact). We will run a 2-hour synthetic pre-warm before start.
- Commercial: No SLA credits will be issued for incidents inside the window if Horizon adheres to rollback/monitoring requirements. If Horizon requests to waive rollback/monitoring, we will need a commercial amendment and potential credits.

Action items:
1) Horizon: sign the addendum (DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/abcd1234) by EOD 7/19 to proceed as scheduled.
2) Redwood: Marissa will finalize addendum PDF (attached and shared) and Legal will do a quick review.
3) Joint: 15-minute standups at 09:00 UTC during the window (calendar invite forthcoming).

We’ll share the finalized PDF after Legal’s review. Looking forward to a smooth test.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-uptime-addendum-v1.pdf
